𝟯𝟬𝗧𝗛 𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗩𝗘𝗥𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗬 𝗢𝗙 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗢𝗭𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗗𝗜𝗦𝗖𝗢 𝗙𝗜𝗥𝗘 🔥

On this day in 1996, more than 160 lives, mostly graduating students for year-end celebrations, were tragically lost in a fire at Ozone Disco in Quezon City. This is considered the 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗶𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝗻 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗻 𝗣𝗵𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗽𝗽𝗶𝗻𝗲 𝗵𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗹𝗱’𝘀 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝗻𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝗰𝗹𝘂𝗯 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀.

The blaze ignited just before midnight, trapping over 300 young patrons and staff inside an overcrowded space. What began as sparks and smoke, mistaken for part of the show, quickly turned into darkness and flames, as blocked exits and locked doors funneled people into a single, fatal choke point.

The tragedy, which occurred during #FirePreventionMonth, exposed a chain of critical failures: inadequate fire safety systems, the absence of proper emergency exits, severe overcrowding, and the deadly consequences of panic.

WTA Miami 

Lulu Sun vs Taylor Townsend

🧠 Form & Context

🇳🇿 Lulu Sun (#111, left-handed)
📉 2026: 4–6 overall | 4–6 on hard
✅ Came through qualifying in Miami with straight-set wins over Maria Timofeeva and Donna Vekic.
🔁 That qualifying run gives her some rhythm and confidence, especially after a stop-start start to the season.
⚠️ Main-draw results have still been patchy, with first-round losses at the Australian Open, Manila, Austin, and Dubai, although she did beat Emma Navarro in Austin before falling to Paula Badosa.

🇺🇸 Taylor Townsend (#80, left-handed, 170 cm)
📈 2026: 9–4 overall | 9–4 on hard
✅ Arrives in much better form after reaching the Austin final and winning matches in Indian Wells qualifying and main draw.
🏠 Miami has generally been a positive event for her, with back-to-back third-round appearances in 2024 and 2025.
💪 Her hard-court level has looked stronger and more stable than Sun’s, and she comes in with more proven tour-level momentum.

🔍 Match Breakdown
This is an interesting lefty-versus-lefty matchup, but Townsend looks to hold the clearer edge in form, match sharpness, and overall hard-court reliability.

Sun deserves credit for coming through Miami qualifying with two very solid wins, especially the straight-set result over Vekic. That gives her valuable court time and some early adaptation to the conditions. The problem for her is that the step from qualifying success to beating an in-form top-80 player is significant, especially against someone who has already shown she can put together deep weeks on hard courts this season.

Townsend has simply been operating at a higher level. Her Austin run to the final stands out, and she backed that up with a convincing win over Marie Bouzkova in Indian Wells before losing to Marta Kostyuk. Compared to Sun, her 2026 hard-court résumé is stronger, and so is her recent consistency.

The head-to-head is also mildly favorable to Townsend, who beat Sun comfortably in Concord back in 2022. That result is not decisive now, but it does reinforce the stylistic idea that Townsend can handle this matchup.

The biggest question for Sun is whether she can extend enough pressure from the baseline after qualifying without letting Townsend dictate too many service patterns and first-strike exchanges. Sun’s best chance is to use her recent momentum, stay aggressive early, and force Townsend into longer stretches of concentration. But if Townsend serves cleanly and controls the front foot of rallies, she should be the one with more scoreboard authority.

🔮 Prediction
Lulu Sun is not arriving empty-handed here. She already has two wins in Miami qualifying, and that gives her a live underdog profile. But Townsend comes in with the better 2026 body of work, deeper hard-court form, stronger tournament history in Miami, and more proven main-tour consistency.

That makes Townsend the deserved favorite. Sun can stay competitive for stretches, especially early, but over the course of the match Townsend looks more likely to absorb pressure, create the bigger moments, and come through.

Prediction: Taylor Townsend

ICYMI O/N 

IRAN:

Iran's stance against the development of nuclear weapons will not significantly change, Foreign Araqchi told Al Jazeera. Araqchi said he believed that after the war comes to an end, countries that border the Gulf should draft a new protocol for the Strait, to ensure that safe passage through the narrow waterway is carried out under certain conditions aligned with Iranian and regional interests. Araqchi said an end to the war was only conceivable if the conflict is permanently over throughout the region and Iran receives compensation for damages incurred. (RTRS)

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Israel's killing of security chief Ali Larijani and other key officials would not hinder its operations with replacements swiftly appointed. Said the U.S. and Israel did not understand that the Islamic Republic was a robust political system and did not depend on any single individual. (RTRS)

Axiso article "Trump aides foresee Iran endgame divide: "Israel doesn't hate the chaos"" cites several US officials describing Trump as the most bullish person in the White House on going to war with Iran, saying he appears more aligned with Netanyahu's maximalist objectives than many of his aides. They say the Strait of Hormuz crisis makes it unlikely the U.S. will seek to pull back any time soon. Stabilizing the global oil market is a bigger priority for the U.S. than for Israel, officials say. (Axios)

Crude exports from Iraq's Kirkuk fields to Turkey's Ceyhan port has resumed via pipeline (300k BPD), North Oil Company sources said to Reuters, after Baghdad and the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) agreed on Tuesday to restart flows. (RTRS)

Iran targeted Tel Aviv with missiles carrying cluster warheads in what it said was retaliation for Israel's assassination of Larijani, Iranian state television reported. Israel has said that Iran has repeatedly used cluster warheads, which disperse into multiple smaller explosives mid-air and spread over a wide area, making them difficult to intercept. (RTRS)

Israeli airstrikes in Beirut killed at least six people on Wednesday, the Lebanese health ministry said, shaking the heart of the Lebanese capital as Israel intensified its offensive against the Iran-backed Hezbollah group. (RTRS)

NATO is deploying additional Patriot battery from Germany at Turkey’s Incirlik Air Base in southern Adana province, state-run Anadolu Agency says. (BBG) 

Iranian state media confirmed the death of Ali Larijani, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and a key pillar of the country’s wartime leadership. (BBG)

Iran has been moving its crude through the Strait of Hormuz at rates broadly comparable to transit before the war began, according to Kpler data, making the most of its control of the vital waterway as other exporters falter. (BBG)

'Gulf States Want the U.S. to Cripple Iranian Regime Before Ending War' WSJ article notes the shift in tone from the UAE and other Persian Gulf states that now view Iran as an existential enemy, seeking its neutralization at the end of the conflict. (WSJ)

'Israel Is Hunting Down Iranian Regime Members in Their Hideouts, One by One' WSJ article profile's Israel method of systematically going after Iran’s leadership and rank-and-file to disrupt the regime’s command and control. (WSJ)

Iran is capable of sharply escalating its campaign against energy infrastructure in the Gulf, analysts have warned. (FT)

As oil traders brace for a historic release from the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve in the form of a loan, they’re dumping prompt barrels and snapping up cheaper supplies further out when borrowers will need to repay the government. (BBG)

China, the world’s biggest crude importer, is close to tapping its vast commercial oil reserves as the Middle East war shows no signs of ending, according to FGE NexantECA, an energy consultant. (BBG)

A Russian oil-laden tanker that was bound for China has U-turned in the South China Sea, and is now hurrying to India after New Delhi began doubling down on imports from Moscow. (BBG)

The conflict in the Middle East has turned the container shipping sector into a “wild west”, with carriers adding thousands of dollars in extra charges and dumping containers at far-flung ports, according to shipping customers and removal companies. (FT)

The Philippines is in discussions with major fertilizer producers including China and Russia to safeguard supply on fears exporters won’t deliver on contracts as the Middle East war keeps prices high. (BBG)

MACRO:

South Korean stocks jumped (KOSPI +5%) after authorities moved to restrict publicly traded companies from listing certain subsidiaries, curbing a practice long blamed for diluting shareholder value. (BBG)

'Powell’s Second-to-Last Meeting Previews an Increasingly Divided Fed' WSJ article by Nick Timiraos highlights as many as three governors are candidates to dissent at this week’s meeting, an unusual break that offers a glimpse of the fracture Kevin Warsh stands to inherit. (WSJ)

Soaring oil prices threaten to hit US growth, worsen inflation and keep the Federal Reserve from lowering interest rates, top economists have warned ahead of the central bank’s first rate decision since the Iran war began. The majority of academic economists polled said that if oil prices were to remain at $100 a barrel, slightly above their current level, US growth will decline markedly. (FT)

Trans Mountain Corp. is planning a series of expansion projects for its main pipeline that will add capacity beginning early next year just as export space out of western Canada becomes tight once again. (BBG)

Pimco Sees Private Credit Strains Triggering Wake-Up Call on Liquidity Risks. (BBG)

The Securities and Exchange Commission issued a long-awaited “token taxonomy” on Tuesday, a key step forward laying out which types of digital assets it deems to be securities. (BBG)

Japanese PM Takaichi visits the White House on Thursday for meetings that offer U.S. President Donald Trump a chance to lean on a key security partner for support in his Iran war, threatening to strain a decades-old alliance. Japanese officials involved in the preparations said Takaichi had hoped to remind Trump of the dangers posed by a regionally assertive China prior to his visit there. (RTRS)

A growing number of hedge funds are positioning for potential hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan as the Iran war amplifies inflation risks in the energy-importing nation. (BBG)

Major Japanese companies, including Toyota, offered big pay hikes in annual wage talks on Wednesday, reflecting strong pay momentum for a fourth consecutive year, although uncertainty from the Middle East conflict clouds the outlook. (RTRS)

Japan's exports rose for a sixth straight month, data showed on Wednesday, pointing to resilient global demand, although industrial supply chain disruptions driven by the Middle East conflict loom as a risk to the world's fourth-largest economy. (RTRS)

Japanese manufacturers' confidence improved to its highest level in over four years in March, buoyed by the chemicals and petroleum sectors and a recovery in the semiconductor market, the Reuters Tankan poll showed. (RTRS)

Japan’s inbound tourism numbers returned to growth in February, as an increase from other regions made up for a continued slump in Chinese tourists. (BBG)

PetroChina Co., the country’s biggest natural gas supplier, will keep its contract prices largely unchanged this year to shield industrial consumers from surging global energy prices due to the Middle East conflict. (BBG)

Aluminum, one of the metals most directly affected by the war in Iran, is struggling to attract buyers in China after prices surged to a four-year high. (BBG)

Chinese companies are boosting hedges through foreign‑exchange derivatives, pushing outstanding forward contracts to record levels, as the yuan’s surge threatens to erode exporters’ overseas earnings. (BBG)

Smaller banks in China are adopting varied strategies in their asset asset allocation as they navigate a volatile bond market, China Securities Journal reports. While some smaller banks are making large purchases of long-term bonds, others are focusing on short-term debt. (CSJ)

Some wealth management products in China have allocated a sizable share of their portfolios to non-standard debt assets in pursuit of higher returns, raising concerns that regulatory limits may be breached. (CSJ)

China Securities Regulatory Commission has recently approved 15 mutual fund products on the same day that track indices related to AI and other emerging industries of strategic importance. (CSJ)

The European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will visit Australia later this month and meet Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, said the Commission on Wednesday, as both sides try to clinch a trade deal. (RTRS)

The BoE may respond more aggressively than expected to soaring energy prices since war broke out in the Middle East because its internal models assume a large and long-lasting impact on inflation. (BBG)

Britain’s resurgent Green Party will call on Prime Minister Keir Starmer to hike taxes on businesses and the wealthy in order to subsidize voters’ household bills, in light of soaring energy prices from the US war on Iran. (BBG)

The Swiss National Bank’s determination to cap gains in the franc will draw the spotlight in a decision that is likely to avoid the more drastic option of negative borrowing costs. (BBG)

New analysis from Australia's Treasury on Wednesday forecast higher inflation and a bigger economic hit from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, that has unleashed a global oil shock and driven up commodity prices. (RTRS)

Libya’s National Oil Corp. reported a fire after a pipeline leak from the country’s largest oil field, according to a statement. Production at Sharara was continuing, with some flows redirected to the El Feel pipeline toward Mellitah port, and the remainder diverted through the Hamada pipeline to the Zawiya storage tanks, the company said. Together, these measures have “significantly reduced” oil losses, it said. (BBG)

South African inflation eased in February, but the central bank is unlikely to view this as a reason to cut interest rates next week as it weighs the impact of conflict in the Middle East. (BBG)

India’s rupee may slump to 95 against the dollar over the next year because of the fallout from the Iran conflict, putting pressure on the central bank to act if inflation picks up, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s chief economist for the country. (BBG)

The Iran war has led to a cooking gas shortage in India, prompting some homemakers to turn to firewood for cooking. (BBG)

The United Arab Emirates’ central bank rolled out a resilience package to support the banking sector and boost liquidity and lending capacity as the fallout from the Iran war ripples through regional markets and dents investor sentiment. (BBG)

Taiwan’s life insurers have cut their holdings of forwards by a notional NT$1.75 trillion ($55 billion) this year after regulatory changes allowed them to spread out the impact of currency fluctuations on their balance sheets. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

China offered on Wednesday what it said would be energy stability to Taiwan if it agreed to Beijing's rule, part of a campaign by China to convince the island of the benefits of "reunification", which it has long rejected. There was no immediate response to the comments from Taiwan's government. (RTRS)

The war on Iran has not delayed shipments of weapons to Taiwan or changed U.S. policy toward the island, officials from President Donald Trump's administration told members of Congress on Tuesday, despite the demands of the intense air campaign. (RTRS)

EQUITIES:

Tencent posted a 13% rise in quarterly revenue, underscoring solid momentum in its core gaming and advertising units while it ramps up a bet on agentic AI. (BBG)

Alibaba is raising prices for its AI computing and storage products by as much as 34%, joining a host of big tech firms moving to capitalize on surging demand in the hope of recouping hefty investments. (BBG)

Chinese shares related to OpenClaw jumped, buoyed by bullish comments from Nvidia Corp.’s chief on the potential of artificial intelligence agents. MiniMax +29%, Knowledge Atlas Technology +23%. Jensen Huang said Tuesday that OpenClaw is “definitely the next ChatGPT,” describing it as a foundational shift that expands what individuals can do with the technology. (BBG)

Nvidia has won Beijing's approval to sell its second-most powerful artificial intelligence chips (H200s) to China and is also preparing a version of the Groq AI chip that can be sold to the Chinese market, according to Reuters sources. (RTRS)

Taiwan shipments of Nvidia Vera Rubin-based servers are expected to begin in the 3rd quarter (Q3) and peak in Q4 this year, media report, adding all the top server makers, Foxconn, Quanta, Wistron, Wiwynn, Inventec, Asustek, Pegatron will offer builds. (UDN Via @dnystedt)

Samsung agreed to supply and collaborate with AMD on next-generation AI memory and computing technologies. Under a preliminary agreement, Samsung will provide next-generation high-bandwidth memory, HBM4, as the primary supplier for AMD’s MI455X accelerators used in corporate data centers. (BBG)

Samsung is considering a shift toward multi-year contracts for memory chips, a much longer timeframe than is typical that may help stabilize supply and ease concerns about a shortage of the essential components. (BBG)

Samsung Electronics' unionised workers in South Korea voted on Wednesday to authorise a strike, deepening a labour dispute over bonuses and raising the risk of production disruptions at the world's biggest memory chipmaker. (RTRS)

Microsoft is weighing legal action against Amazon and OpenAI over a $50bn deal that could breach its exclusive cloud partnership with the ChatGPT maker, setting up a clash between the Big Tech rivals. The dispute centres on whether AWS can offer OpenAI’s new commercial product, Frontier, without violating a longstanding agreement that requires all access to the start-up’s models to be routed through Microsoft’s Azure cloud platform. (FT)

JPMorgan Chase and Wall Street banks suspended more than $5bn of debt sales for customer service software group Qualtrics amid investor scepticism over whether its business model can withstand AI disruption. (FT)

Amazon is planning to sharply cut the number of packages it ships through the U.S. Postal Service, a move that could cost the agency billions of dollars in much-needed revenue. (WSJ)

Meta has repeatedly failed to stop illegal ads for high-risk financial products running on its platforms in Britain, despite committing to block them, according to a review by the country's financial regulator. (RTRS)

Banks prepare to offload $18bn in debt tied to EA take-private deal. (FT)

The world’s largest oil and gas companies ratcheted back investment in the energy transition in 2025, marking the first annual decline in eight years, according to BloombergNEF. (BBG)

Sumitomo Life Insurance Co. is considering allocating about ¥300 billion ($1.9 billion) on private credit in the fiscal year starting April, in the latest push by a Japanese financial firm into alternative assets to boost returns. (BBG)

Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. has reached out to Asian banks backing an around $1.5 billion Saudi loan deal to reconfirm their commitments, an unusual step highlighting the risks the conflict in Iran poses for lending in the region. (BBG)

Elliott Investment Management has built a stake in Mitsui O.S.K., saying the Japanese shipping giant is materially undervalued despite its business strength, the latest in a series of activist moves targeting prominent Japanese companies. (WSJ)

Geely Automobile Holdings Ltd.’s full-year profit beat analyst estimates and climbed to a record as China’s second-largest carmaker closed in on market leader BYD Co.’s sales, thanks to the popularity of its EX2 hatchbacks and Zeekr sport utility vehicles. (BBG)

BHP Group named Brandon Craig as its next CEO, opting for his experience in advancing the company’s growth projects in the U.S., Canada and South America as the world’s biggest miner expands in copper and the fertilizer ingredient potash. (WSJ)

A cargo of BHP's Jimblebar Fines iron ore is heading to India in a rare sale driven by discounts on the product that was banned for sale in China, the world's largest buyer, as part of a contract dispute with the miner, Reuters reports. (RTRS)

United Co. Rusal International PJSC recorded its first annual loss in more than a decade, hit by a strong ruble and surging borrowing costs. (BBG)
